\chapter{Learning Theory --- Johnson--Lindenstrauss Main}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.LearningTheory.JohnsonLindenstrauss.Main
\section{Overview}

This module assembles the complete Johnson--Lindenstrauss flattening lemma.
Starting from the distortion predicate and the bad-event definitions, it
applies a Gaussian (or sub-Gaussian Rademacher) concentration bound and a
union bound to show, via the probabilistic method, that for any finite set
$V \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ of at most $n$ points and any $0 < \varepsilon < 1$,
a random $k \times d$ matrix with $k \ge 32 \log n / \varepsilon^2$ rows is,
with positive probability, an $\varepsilon$-JL embedding of $V$; it then
extracts the deterministic witness and provides both squared-distance and
distance-form corollaries together with explicit logarithmic dimension bounds.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Single-pair distortion bound]
\lean{JLDistortion}
\label{JLDistortion}
\leanok
For $\varepsilon \in \mathbb{R}$, vectors $u, v \in \mathbb{R}^d$, and their
images $u', v' \in \mathbb{R}^k$, \texttt{JLDistortion} asserts the two-sided
squared-distance inequality
\[
  (1 - \varepsilon)\,\|u - v\|^2 \;\le\; \|u' - v'\|^2 \;\le\;
  (1 + \varepsilon)\,\|u - v\|^2.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[$\varepsilon$-JL embedding]
\lean{IsJLEmbedding}
\label{IsJLEmbedding}
\leanok
\uses{JLDistortion}
A linear map $f : \mathbb{R}^d \to_L[\mathbb{R}] \mathbb{R}^k$ is an
\emph{$\varepsilon$-JL embedding} of a finite set $V$ if, for every ordered
pair $(u, v) \in V \times V$, the pair $(f(u), f(v))$ satisfies
\texttt{JLDistortion} $\varepsilon\; u\; v$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Bad-pair event]
\lean{BadPair}
\label{BadPair}
\leanok
\uses{JLDistortion}
Given a $k \times d$ matrix $A$ and a finite set
$V \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$, \texttt{BadPair} $\varepsilon\; V\; A$ holds when
there exists some ordered pair $(u, v) \in V \times V$ whose images under $A$
fail the distortion predicate, i.e.\ the projection distorts that pair by
more than a factor of $\varepsilon$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[JL concentration --- single vector]
\lean{jl_concentration_single}
\label{jl_concentration_single}
\leanok
\uses{BadSingle, jl_concentration_single_via_chi_squared}
\difficulty{1}
Let $A$ be a random $k \times d$ matrix whose entries are i.i.d.\
$\mathcal{N}(0, 1/k)$ (rows mutually independent, entries independent within
each row).  For any fixed $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$ and any $0 < \varepsilon < 1$,
\[
  \Pr\bigl[\text{BadSingle}\;\varepsilon\;A\;x\bigr] \;\le\;
  2\,\exp\!\bigl(-k\varepsilon^2/8\bigr).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Distortion from non-bad single]
\lean{JLDistortion.of_not_bad}
\label{JLDistortion.of_not_bad}
\leanok
\uses{BadSingle, JLDistortion}
\difficulty{3}
If the matrix $A$ does \emph{not} trigger the bad-single event for the
difference $u - v$, then \texttt{JLDistortion} $\varepsilon\; u\; v\;
(A.toEuclideanLin\; u)\; (A.toEuclideanLin\; v)$ holds; that is, the
squared-distance of the images is within a factor of $(1 \pm \varepsilon)$
of the squared-distance of the originals.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[JL union bound]
\lean{jl_union_bound}
\label{jl_union_bound}
\leanok
\uses{BadPair, BadSingle, JLDistortion.of_not_bad}
\difficulty{5}
Suppose each per-pair bad event satisfies
$\Pr[\text{BadSingle}\;\varepsilon\;A\;\cdot] \le 2\exp(-k\varepsilon^2/8)$.
Then the probability that \emph{some} ordered pair in $V \times V$ is
distorted is at most
\[
  |V|^2 \cdot 2\,\exp\!\bigl(-k\varepsilon^2/8\bigr).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Structural JL --- Gaussian probabilistic method]
\lean{johnson_lindenstrauss_of_gaussian}
\label{johnson_lindenstrauss_of_gaussian}
\leanok
\uses{BadPair, BadSingle, IsJLEmbedding, jl_concentration_single, jl_union_bound}
\difficulty{4}
Let $A$ be a random Gaussian $k \times d$ matrix as above.  If the union-bound
failure probability satisfies
$|V|^2 \cdot 2\exp(-k\varepsilon^2/8) < 1$,
then there exists a linear map $f : \mathbb{R}^d \to_L \mathbb{R}^k$ that is an
$\varepsilon$-JL embedding of $V$, extracted from the positive-measure good
event.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Structural JL --- sub-Gaussian probabilistic method]
\lean{johnson_lindenstrauss_of_subgaussian}
\label{johnson_lindenstrauss_of_subgaussian}
\leanok
\uses{BadPair, BadSingle, IsJLEmbedding, concentration_zero, jl_concentration_single_subgaussian, jl_union_bound}
\difficulty{4}
Sub-Gaussian analogue of \texttt{johnson\_lindenstrauss\_of\_gaussian}: the Gaussian
entry hypotheses are replaced by the assumptions that each row projection
$(Ax)_i$ is sub-Gaussian with parameter $\|x\|^2/k$ and has variance exactly
$\|x\|^2/k$.  Under the same failure-probability bound
$|V|^2 \cdot 2\exp(-k\varepsilon^2/8) < 1$, an $\varepsilon$-JL embedding of
$V$ is guaranteed to exist; this covers, for instance, Rademacher ($\pm 1/\sqrt{k}$)
matrices.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Measurability of bad-single event]
\lean{measurableSet_badSingle}
\label{measurableSet_badSingle}
\leanok
\uses{BadSingle}
\difficulty{4}
For any measurable map $A : \Omega \to \mathrm{Matrix}(\mathrm{Fin}\,k,
\mathrm{Fin}\,d,\mathbb{R})$, fixed $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$, and $\varepsilon \in
\mathbb{R}$, the set $\{\omega \mid \text{BadSingle}\;\varepsilon\;(A\,\omega)\;x\}$
is measurable.  The key step is that each coordinate map
$\omega \mapsto (A\,\omega \cdot \text{toEuclideanLin}\; x)_i$ is measurable, hence
so is the squared norm.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Existence of i.i.d.\ Gaussian matrix]
\lean{exists_iid_gaussian_matrix}
\label{exists_iid_gaussian_matrix}
\leanok
\difficulty{6}
For any $k > 0$ and $d \ge 0$, there exists a probability space
$(\Omega, \mathcal{F}, \mu)$ carrying a measurable random matrix
$A : \Omega \to \mathrm{Matrix}(\mathrm{Fin}\,k, \mathrm{Fin}\,d, \mathbb{R})$
whose entries are i.i.d.\ $\mathcal{N}(0, 1/k)$, with rows mutually independent
and entries within each row jointly independent.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Numerical failure-probability bound]
\lean{jl_failure_bound_of_dim}
\label{jl_failure_bound_of_dim}
\leanok
\difficulty{5}
Given $0 < \varepsilon$, $n \ge 2$, $k \ge 32 \log n / \varepsilon^2$, and
$|V| \le n$, this lemma derives (i) $k > 0$ and (ii)
$|V|^2 \cdot 2\exp(-k\varepsilon^2/8) < 1$, the numerical precondition
consumed by both \texttt{johnson\_lindenstrauss\_of\_gaussian} and
\texttt{johnson\_lindenstrauss\_of\_subgaussian}.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Johnson--Lindenstrauss flattening lemma (Gaussian)]
\lean{johnson_lindenstrauss}
\label{johnson_lindenstrauss}
\leanok
\uses{BadSingle, IsJLEmbedding, exists_iid_gaussian_matrix, jl_failure_bound_of_dim, johnson_lindenstrauss_of_gaussian, measurableSet_badSingle}
\difficulty{2}
For any $0 < \varepsilon < 1$, $n \ge 2$, $k \ge 32 \log n / \varepsilon^2$,
and any finite set $V \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ of at most $n$ points, there
exists a linear map $f : \mathbb{R}^d \to_L \mathbb{R}^k$ that is an
$\varepsilon$-JL embedding of $V$, i.e.\ it satisfies
$(1 - \varepsilon)\|u-v\|^2 \le \|f(u)-f(v)\|^2 \le (1+\varepsilon)\|u-v\|^2$
for all $u, v \in V$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Johnson--Lindenstrauss flattening lemma (sub-Gaussian)]
\lean{johnson_lindenstrauss_subgaussian}
\label{johnson_lindenstrauss_subgaussian}
\leanok
\uses{BadSingle, IsJLEmbedding, hasSubgaussianMGF_row_proj, integral_sq_row_proj, jl_failure_bound_of_dim, johnson_lindenstrauss_of_subgaussian, measurableSet_badSingle, measurable_radMatrix, radJointMeasure, radMatrix, radMatrix_proj_indep, radMatrix_proj_meas}
\difficulty{3}
Rademacher ($\pm 1/\sqrt{k}$ entries) analogue of \texttt{johnson\_lindenstrauss}:
same hypotheses on $\varepsilon$, $n$, $k$, and $V$, same conclusion---an
$\varepsilon$-JL embedding of $V$ exists---but now realized by a Rademacher
matrix.  The proof uses the sub-Gaussian concentration bound
\texttt{jl\_concentration\_single\_subgaussian} (which inherits the Hanson-Wright
axiom) and the identical union-bound argument.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Distance form of embedding]
\lean{jl_dist_of_embedding}
\label{jl_dist_of_embedding}
\leanok
\uses{IsJLEmbedding, JLDistortion}
\difficulty{4}
If $f$ is an $\varepsilon$-JL embedding of $V$ (in the squared-distance sense),
then for all $u, v \in V$,
\[
  \sqrt{1-\varepsilon}\,\|u - v\| \;\le\; \|f(u) - f(v)\| \;\le\;
  \sqrt{1+\varepsilon}\,\|u - v\|,
\]
obtained by taking square roots of the \texttt{JLDistortion} bounds.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[JL flattening --- distance form (Gaussian)]
\lean{johnson_lindenstrauss_dist}
\label{johnson_lindenstrauss_dist}
\leanok
\uses{jl_dist_of_embedding, johnson_lindenstrauss}
\difficulty{1}
Under the same hypotheses as \texttt{johnson\_lindenstrauss}, there exists a linear
map $f : \mathbb{R}^d \to_L \mathbb{R}^k$ such that for all $u, v \in V$,
\[
  \sqrt{1-\varepsilon}\,\|u - v\| \;\le\; \|f(u) - f(v)\| \;\le\;
  \sqrt{1+\varepsilon}\,\|u - v\|.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[JL flattening --- distance form (sub-Gaussian)]
\lean{johnson_lindenstrauss_subgaussian_dist}
\label{johnson_lindenstrauss_subgaussian_dist}
\leanok
\uses{jl_dist_of_embedding, johnson_lindenstrauss_subgaussian}
\difficulty{1}
Under the same hypotheses as \texttt{johnson\_lindenstrauss\_subgaussian}, there
exists a linear map $f : \mathbb{R}^d \to_L \mathbb{R}^k$ satisfying the same
two-sided distance-ratio bounds as \texttt{johnson\_lindenstrauss\_dist}, now
realized by a Rademacher random matrix.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Logarithmic dimension bound (Gaussian)]
\lean{johnson_lindenstrauss_dim_bound}
\label{johnson_lindenstrauss_dim_bound}
\leanok
\uses{IsJLEmbedding, johnson_lindenstrauss}
\difficulty{2}
For any $0 < \varepsilon < 1$ and $n \ge 2$, there exists a threshold
$k_0 \in \mathbb{N}$ such that for every $k \ge k_0$, every ambient
dimension $d$, and every set $V \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ of at most $n$ points,
an $\varepsilon$-JL embedding $f : \mathbb{R}^d \to_L \mathbb{R}^k$ of $V$
exists.  In particular the target dimension is $O(\log n / \varepsilon^2)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Logarithmic dimension bound (sub-Gaussian)]
\lean{johnson_lindenstrauss_subgaussian_dim_bound}
\label{johnson_lindenstrauss_subgaussian_dim_bound}
\leanok
\uses{IsJLEmbedding, johnson_lindenstrauss_subgaussian}
\difficulty{2}
Sub-Gaussian (Rademacher) analogue of \texttt{johnson\_lindenstrauss\_dim\_bound}:
same threshold $k_0 = O(\log n / \varepsilon^2)$, same universal conclusion for
all $k \ge k_0$, $d$, and $V$ of size at most $n$, but inheriting the
Hanson-Wright axiom from the sub-Gaussian concentration chain.
\end{theorem}
